findings.evidence: kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the consent, not to the profile: when a member turns birthday greetings off, clear `birthday` and `phone` on their profile (Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 7(3) withdrawal of consent). Add an opt-out requirement and scenario to the spec ("WHEN a member opts out THEN their birthday and phone are erased") and a task with its test. Today a member who opts out keeps both fields stored for as long as the account lives, with no purpose left for them.
findings.title: Birthday and phone are kept after the member opts out

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: State how long the nightly backups keep these columns and how an erasure (opt-out or account deletion) reaches them — for example a bounded backup rotation after which erased values are gone, or a re-applied erasure on restore. The backup retention policy may exist outside this plan; the design should cite it.
findings.title: Retention of birthday and phone in the nightly backups is undefined

findings.evidence: phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Identify Textly as a processor and the transfer outside the EEA: name the data processing agreement (Art. 28) and the Chapter V mechanism (adequacy decision / EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification, or standard contractual clauses), and Textly's own retention of the phone numbers and messages it receives. Question for the team: only the controller can tell whether these are in place.
findings.title: Textly, a US-hosted processor, has no stated processing agreement or transfer safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: State the purpose (birthday greetings only, no other marketing use of the phone number) and the lawful basis — presumably consent through the opt-in, Art. 6(1)(a) — in the proposal, so the birthday and phone are not reused for other marketing campaigns. Question for the team: only the controller can confirm the basis.
findings.title: Lawful basis and purpose of the new data are not stated
